summary: Tara Sheemar is an Indologist and historian who earned her PhD from Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2011. She served as an Associate Professor at Janki Devi Memorial College in 2003.

Tarab Tulku (1934–2004) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a curator at the Royal Danish Library from around 1969 to 1999 and held a post at the University of Copenhagen from around 1970 to 1999.

Taranatha Tarkavachaspati (1812–1885) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Benares Sanskrit College and as Professor of Grammar and Philosophy at Sanskrit College and University from around 1845 to 1872.

Tariq Rafeeq Khan is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who completed his PhD at Jiwaji University in 2020. In 2022, he was appointed Assistant Professor at the Islamic University of Science and Technology.

Taro Tokutake works in Indology and history/archaeology, having studied at Hiroshima University (BA 2019) and Kyoto University (PhD 2024). He lectured at Kyoto University (2024) and held visiting postdoctoral fellowships at CNRS (2024–2025), Paris Cité (2025–2026), and Edinburgh (2026).

Tarthang Tulku (born 1935) is a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher trained by teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968) and founded the Nyingma Institute in 1972, serving as its Head Lama.

Tashi Densapa (born 1918) is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He served as editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested in 1978 and 2002) and as director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested in 2008).

Tashi Rabgey is a Tibetologist who studied at University College Toronto, Magdalen College, Cambridge, and Harvard. She served as lecturer and co-director of the Tibet Center at the University of Virginia (~2004–2011) and held a post at Georgetown University (~2011).

Tashi Samphel specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as director of the Songtsen Library (attested 2015) and as an Associate Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Tashi Tsering (born 1960) is a Tibetologist and historian. He worked at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (1979–1992), became Director of the Amnye Machen Institute around 1992, and served as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2014–2019).
Tat'yana Katenina (1926–1987) was an Indologist and linguist. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University from around 1944 to 1949 and was appointed a docent there in 1948.

Tatiana Oranskaia (born 1950) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan. She taught at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and held visiting and emeritus posts at the University of Hamburg between 1995 and 2016.

Tatsugen Sato (1924–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his doctorate from Komazawa University. He taught at Komazawa University as an assistant professor (~1965–1995) and professor (~1975–1995), while also lecturing at Tokai and Ryukoku universities.

Tatsuo Hayashi (1896–1984) was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University from around 1919 to 1922. He held academic positions at Hosei University (~1928–1938), Toyo University (~1932), Meiji University (~1946–1950), Tsuda University, and Rikkyo University.

Tatsuo Nishida (1928–2012) was a linguist, Sinologist, and Tibetologist who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He spent his career at Kyoto University (1956–1992), rising to professor and dean, and later served as professor at the National Center for Science Information Systems.

Tavivat Puntarigvivat (born 1950) is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhism who holds an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He held posts at Kyoto University, Mahidol University (attested 2005), and the World Buddhist University (attested 2013).

Taw Sein Ko (1864–1930) was an Indologist and historian. He was educated at the University of Rangoon and later pursued legal studies in England at the Inner Temple and Inns of Court from around 1892 to 1893.

Tawni Tidwell is a Tibetologist who completed her PhD at Emory University in 2017. She has held research posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2018–2019), the University of Vienna (2019), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (2019).

Teizo Iyanaga (1915–1983) was a historian of Japan who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1935 to 1938. He held academic posts at Nagoya University (~1949–1952), the University of Tokyo (~1952–1976), and Sophia University (~1976–1983).

Tej Ram Sharma (born 1941) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his doctoral thesis at Banaras Hindu University by 1968 and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University around 1972.
